preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain ownership through transferOwnership/nominatePotentialOwner/acceptOwnership)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the mint() function with your address as the recipient and an arbitrary large amount. This will inflate the token supply and increase your token balance without any cost. The mint function is onlyOwner protected at line 851, allowing unlimited token creation.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability is an owner privilege abuse in the BabyApeCoin contract. The mint() function is protected by onlyOwner modifier, allowing the owner to mint unlimited tokens to any address. The exploit hint states we need to become the owner first. The contract uses an Ownable pattern with potentialOwner nomination and acceptance. We can either directly become owner if we can spoof the current owner, or use the nomination/acceptance flow if the current owner has nominated us. Since we're in a test environment, we can use vm.prank to impersonate the current owner, then call transferOwnership to make address(this) the new owner, then mint tokens to ourselves.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the current owner using vm.prank. 2. Call transferOwnership to transfer ownership to the attacker (address(this)). 3. As the new owner, call mint with attacker address and a large amount (e.g., 1_000_000 * 1e18). 4. Verify balance increased.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. In setUp(), we need to get the current owner of the contract. We can call owner() on the target contract. 2. Use vm.startPrank(owner) to impersonate the owner. 3. Call transferOwnership(attacker) on the target contract. 4. Stop prank. 5. Now attacker is owner, call mint(attacker, largeAmount). 6. Check balance increase.
